documents.text:
Name: Artisans Guild
Type: faction
Summary: A national guild representing skilled crafts and productive trades in West.
The Artisans Guild encompasses many artisan professions rather than a separate major national faction for each craft. It may maintain local city branches with local representatives, who collectively determine or select a national representative. Selection methods remain undefined. Branches are parts of this national institution. Specialized local associations may emerge later; none are authored now.

Name: Beastfolk
Type: world_lore
Summary: Beastfolk are a broad umbrella of animal-associated lineages; prejudice against them is common in human-dominated West.
Possible lineages include feline, canine, vulpine, lupine, and other familiar variants; this list is non-exhaustive. Human-dominated society in West commonly treats Beastfolk as socially inferior. This is West social prejudice, not biological truth. Beastfolk there are disproportionately found among enslaved populations, agricultural labor, hard manual work, combat-related exploitation, and vulnerable social classes. Not every Beastfolk is enslaved. This social pattern is not universal across the world; Center, East, and future continents may have different relationships with Beastfolk, presently undefined.

Name: Blackwater
Aliases: The Unchained Haven
Type: location
Parent: West
Summary: Blackwater, The Unchained Haven, is a criminal maritime enclave on West's southwestern coast, outside effective normal direct West control.
Its dark coastal/cliff environment supports a persistent maritime criminal culture. Conventional state governance is weak or absent, but power exists in fragmented, unstable competition among smuggling interests, pirate captains, and criminal cartels. Black-market commerce includes fencing stolen goods, illegal slave traffic, transfer or sale of unregistered or stolen captives, and people kidnapped from neighboring nations. Geographic containment in West does not imply effective direct political control. Calderan dislikes and distrusts Blackwater but pragmatically tolerates some of its existence for dirty economic value, absorption of crime, indirect maritime defense/interdiction, and keeping worse external threats at distance. Tolerance is not lawful endorsement or a formal treaty. Blackwater's persistent maritime/commercial rivalry with Sandspear involves Sorrow Sea and Chained Bay routes, smuggling, piracy/corsair activity, protection rackets, captured cargo, slave traffic, and wartime spoils. Their ships sometimes fight bloody naval engagements; this is not formal West–Center naval war, and no winner is predetermined.
Feature: de facto autonomy. Outside effective normal direct West control, despite geographic containment within West.
Feature: fragmented criminal governance. Competing smuggling interests, pirate captains, and criminal cartels exercise unstable power; no formal council is established.
Feature: illegal maritime trade. Black-market trade, stolen goods, kidnapping, and illegal/unregistered slave traffic.
Feature: maritime rival. Sandspear

Name: Calderan
Type: location
Parent: West
Summary: Calderan is West's inland capital, main political center, and main campaign city.
Context: Calderan capital and main campaign city of West.
Calderan lies in the northern/central-western interior of West. The established five-district model applies here: West, East, North, South, and Center are predominant social/economic themes, not exclusive zoning. Existing civic arrangements include the Duke and local council, national guild branches, Church representation, City Guard, and magistracy. The Duke remains central to local civic authority; the relationship between the capital's civic administration and the Crown is not elaborated further. Calderan and Davenport together hold principal institutional/legal control over West's slave market. The full legal constitution of that monopoly remains undefined. Calderan regards Blackwater as a politically awkward necessary evil: disliked and distrusted but pragmatically tolerated for dirty economic value, absorption of crime, indirect maritime defense/interdiction, and keeping worse external threats at distance. This is not blanket lawful endorsement or an established treaty.
Feature: capital of West. West's principal national political center.
Feature: five-district civic structure. West, East, North, South, and Center Districts retain their established non-exclusive themes and civic institutions.
Feature: legal slave-market control. Calderan and Davenport share principal institutional monopoly/control over West's legal slave market.

Name: Calderan Slave Market
Aliases: West District slave pens; Calderan slave pens
Type: location
Parent: Calderan
Summary: Calderan Slave Market is the capital's public, legal slave market and holding pens in Calderan's West District.
Context: Calderan Slave Market: slave market, slave pen, slave pens, where slaves are held, displayed and sold, West District of Calderan.
Calderan Slave Market is a public, legal slave market in Calderan's West District. Enslaved people are held in its pens and displayed there for inspection and sale under West's legal slave trade. Its location is publicly known in Calderan; ordinary citizens could plausibly direct someone to it. No layout, size, owners, operators, or history are established.
Feature: slave pens. Pens where enslaved people are held before display and sale.
Feature: public sale area. A public area where enslaved people are displayed for inspection and sold.

Name: Center
Display name: Center (nation)
Type: location
Parent: Known Continent
Summary: Center is the central, broadly arid and desert-dominated nation; Zul-Rath is its capital.
Context: Center nation on the known continent, distinct from Calderan's Center District.
Center directly borders West and East. Its major mapped settlements are Zul-Rath, Khar-Dune, and Sandspear, without excluding other settlements. The Dragon's Teeth Mountains complicate passage across northern portions of the Center–East transition. West–Center violence is concentrated around their frontier, rather than permanent formally declared total war. Zul-Rath may employ or tolerate Sandspear corsairs when useful. Khar-Dune's underground markets and Sandspear's maritime groups do not establish Center's complete government. Its ruler, political system, religion, and internal institutions remain otherwise undefined; West's monarchy and guild structure are not assigned to it.
Feature: national capital. Zul-Rath
Feature: land border with West. Center directly borders West.
Feature: land border with East. Center directly borders East.
Feature: arid regional climate. Broadly arid and desert-dominated; not a uniform climate rule.

Name: Chained Bay
Type: location
Summary: Chained Bay is a large southwestern bay or inlet, especially associated with West's maritime region.
Davenport lies farther south in West near Chained Bay. Khar-Dune lies relatively near the bay region in western/southwestern Center. Blackwater and Sandspear compete around its maritime routes. These are broad spatial and commercial relationships, not an authored navigation graph. The bay's name has no established supernatural meaning.

Name: Church
Type: faction
Summary: The Church is a powerful national institution in West, distinct from the three national guilds.
The Church has local presence, national representation, political influence, and representation in major civic and national deliberations. It is not a guild, although it has comparable political weight. Its theology, gods, exact ecclesiastical hierarchy, supreme religious office, denominations, particular temples, and doctrine remain undefined. The Inquisition is an organ of the Church.

Name: City Guard
Type: faction
Summary: Calderan's City Guard is a local civic/security faction.
Its responsibilities broadly include local order, patrols, ordinary law enforcement, and urban security. It is distinct from the national guilds and Church, and is not the national military. Full ranks, named members, and specific installations remain undefined.

Name: City Magistracy
Type: concept
Summary: Calderan's civic administration comprises magistrates, clerks, officials, record keepers, and administrative authorities.
Civic administration can influence property, petitions, permits, records, disputes, regulations, and administrative decisions affecting citizens. Magistrates may compete without any specific rivalry or plot being established. This apparatus may overlap socially or professionally with the Learned Arts Guild, but is not a formal subordinate branch, and not every magistrate is a guild member. It is not a Bureaucrats Guild or a single unified autonomous faction. No specific officials or historical playthrough characters are established.

Name: Known Continent
Type: location
Summary: An enormous known continent comprises West, Center, and East, arranged from west to east.
Context: Known continent; geographic parent of the three nations.
The continent is conceptually comparable to Eurasia in scale, without exact dimensions or travel times. West occupies the western portion, Center the central portion, and East the eastern portion. West borders Center, and Center borders East; West and East share no direct land border. Mist Sea lies broadly north, Sorrow Sea west, and The Silent Ocean east. Chained Bay is a large southwestern inlet especially associated with West's maritime region. The Dragon's Teeth Mountains span the northern interior around the Center–East transition. The named major cities are not an exhaustive settlement census.
Feature: continental nations. West, Center, East

Name: Continental Structure
Type: world_lore
Summary: One enormous known continent contains the major geopolitical regions/nations West, Center, and East.
The known continent is conceptually Eurasia-scale, with no exact dimensions, area, or travel times. West, Center, and East occupy its western, central, and eastern portions. West borders Center; Center borders East; West and East share no direct land border. West is broadly mild, temperate, and greener; Center arid and desert-dominated; East cold and snowy with severe winters. These are regional tendencies. Their capitals are Calderan, Zul-Rath, and Vaelrost respectively. Mist Sea lies north, Sorrow Sea west, The Silent Ocean east, and Chained Bay around the southwest. The Dragon's Teeth Mountains span the northern interior near the Center–East transition and Frostspire. West–Center tension is not perpetual declared total war: border skirmishes, raids, territorial incidents, feuds, localized clashes, and unofficial frontier violence can produce captives, displaced civilians, raided villages, prisoners, and slave trafficking. Not every enslaved person is a Center captive. Center's internal government remains undefined. East enforces armed neutrality against spillover from that conflict, notably through Frostspire. East's internal government, religion, peoples, internal factions, and foreign policy beyond this stance remain undefined. No other continent is established.

Name: Davenport
Aliases: The Port of Chains
Type: location
Parent: West
Summary: Davenport, The Port of Chains, is West's principal economic and maritime city, a major port farther south near Chained Bay.
Davenport has an elaborate, wealthy urban presentation, substantial stone docks, and major warehouse infrastructure. It is fundamental to West's maritime economy, with prosperity deeply tied to legal/institutional slave trade. Calderan and Davenport together hold principal institutional monopoly/control over West's legal slave market; detailed law remains undefined. Traffic arrives through frontier markets, Ironbound, Khar-Dune-related networks, and other legally processed sources. Large storage facilities in its warehouse system form part of the logistics chain before auctions or onward transport. Merchant vessels may carry enslaved people toward inland plantations, colonies, or other destinations in West's economic sphere. Plantations and colonies exist somewhere in that broader system, but their locations, sizes, ownership, crops, and political status remain undefined.
Feature: principal economic and maritime port. West's major maritime commercial center, with an elaborate and wealthy urban presentation.
Feature: stone docks and warehouses. Substantial stone docks and major warehouses, including large facilities in slave-trade logistics before auctions or onward transport.
Feature: legal slave-market control. Davenport and Calderan share principal institutional monopoly/control over West's legal slave market.

Name: The Dragon's Teeth Mountains
Type: location
Parent: Known Continent
Summary: A major northern interior mountain chain spans the transition between Center and East, forming a geographic barrier near Frostspire.
The range extends broadly across the northern continental interior rather than forming one isolated peak. It separates or complicates passage between portions of Center and East and lies near Frostspire. Exact elevations, length, peaks, passes, mountain settlements, and the origin of its name remain unspecified. Its name does not establish dragons or a dragon history.
Feature: northern geographic barrier. The extended mountain chain complicates passage across portions of the Center–East transition.

Name: Dwarves
Type: world_lore
Summary: Dwarves are a familiar established people with strong cultural associations with skilled material work.
Craftsmanship, construction, technical trades, and skilled material work are cultural patterns, not biological absolutes. Not every dwarf is an artisan. No racial stat bonuses or dwarf nation are established.

Name: East
Display name: East (nation)
Type: location
Parent: Known Continent
Summary: East is the cold, snowy eastern nation with capital Vaelrost and an armed-neutral stance toward the West–Center conflict.
Context: East nation on the known continent, distinct from Calderan's East District.
East directly borders Center and shares no direct land border with West. Snow and severe winter conditions characterize the region broadly, without requiring uniform conditions. Vaelrost is the capital; Frostspire and Skardgard are other major mapped settlements, not an exhaustive census. East maintains strong neutrality toward West–Center conflict and seeks to prevent its violence from entering East. Frontier forces may repel armed groups or incursions from either side. Frostspire helps enforce this policy. Armed neutrality does not establish pacifism, friendship, or an alliance with either nation. East's internal government, ruler, culture, religion, and broader foreign policy remain undefined.
Feature: national capital. Vaelrost
Feature: land border with Center. East directly borders Center.
Feature: armed neutrality. Frontier forces enforce neutrality toward the West–Center conflict, repelling incursions regardless of origin when necessary.
Feature: cold regional climate. Broadly cold and snowy with severe winters; not uniform everywhere.

Name: Elemental Magic
Type: world_lore
Summary: Fire, Water, Earth, and Air are the four common foundational magical elements and principal known elemental traditions.
Elemental interactions can involve affinities, natural advantages, disadvantages, opposition, and situational strengths. Their relationships are contextual rather than a universal deterministic cycle or combat chart.

Name: Elves
Type: world_lore
Summary: Elves are less common than humans or dwarves, noticeable but not mythical.
Elves are somewhat socially and culturally apart. Enslaved elves may exist but are relatively uncommon. Exact lifespan, biological bonuses, a nation or fixed homeland, universal personality, and a complete culture remain undefined.

Name: Frostspire
Type: location
Parent: East
Summary: Frostspire is an iron-and-coal mining center and military frontier garrison in western/northwestern East near the Dragon's Teeth Mountains.
Near the Center–East frontier zone, Frostspire stands on a rocky spur, dominated by a tall fortified keep surrounded by snowy peaks. Its dual role combines major mining with military frontier duty. Patrols actively prevent West–Center violence from spreading into East, helping enforce strong regional armed neutrality. Frontier forces may repel incursions or armed groups regardless of which side they originate from. This establishes neither an alliance nor friendship with West or Center, and does not define East's entire foreign policy.
Feature: rocky spur and fortified keep. A tall fortified keep dominates the settlement on a rocky spur amid snowy peaks.
Feature: iron and coal mining. Major mining activity extracts iron and coal.
Feature: military frontier garrison. Patrols prevent West–Center violence from entering East.
Feature: armed neutrality. Frostspire enforces East's neutral stance toward the West–Center conflict, repelling incursions from either side when necessary.

Name: Heartstone
Type: location
Parent: Calderan
Summary: Heartstone is an old, tall private residential tower of predominantly stone construction. It is vertically organized, structurally solid, and associated with a secluded walled courtyard.
Context: Heartstone residential stone tower, upper floors, underground level, living floor, secluded courtyard.
Heartstone is a private residence. Its old stone tower construction is partly accented by projecting wooden architectural sections and narrow arched tower windows. The structure remains solid despite its age. The known organization consists of U1 underground, LR at ground level, F1 through F6 rising above LR, and CY, the secluded courtyard. F6 is the highest currently known floor. U1 has a broader underground footprint than the tower floors above. A single continuous spiral staircase rises from LR through F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, and F6. This staircase begins at LR's perimeter and rises along or near the outer portion of the tower interior, reaching each upper floor from the side. It is lateral/peripheral, not a central tower core, leaving each upper floor's central usable area comparatively open. U1 is reached separately through a large visible hatch in LR and descending access, not through the upper-floor spiral staircase.
Feature: stone tower construction. Old, predominantly stone construction forming a tall, vertically organized private residence; structurally solid.
Feature: projecting wooden sections. Projecting wooden architectural sections accent parts of the stone exterior.
Feature: narrow arched tower windows. Narrow arched windows characterize the tower exterior; the total exterior window count is unspecified.
Feature: continuous spiral staircase. A single continuous lateral/peripheral spiral staircase begins at LR's perimeter and rises near the outer tower interior through F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, and F6. It reaches each floor from the side, leaving central usable areas comparatively open; it is not a central core and does not provide access to U1.

Name: Heartstone Courtyard
Display name: Heartstone CY
Aliases: Heartstone secluded courtyard; CY
Type: location
Parent: Heartstone
Summary: Heartstone CY is the tower's secluded outdoor courtyard, enclosed by stone walls and connected directly to LR. It provides space for training, medicinal planting beds, and practical outdoor work.
Context: Heartstone CY secluded walled courtyard, outdoor training, medicinal beds, practical work area.
The secluded courtyard is directly associated with Heartstone's tower and enclosed by stone walls, wrapping around part of the tower base. A normal door connects it directly to LR, distinct from Heartstone's main exterior entrance. Its training area occupies open space farther from the tower and contains training dummies. Two distinct medicinal planting areas contain beds intended for medicinal plants and are initially empty. A garden/tool shed serves gardening and general outdoor tool storage without a specified initial inventory. A practical work table supports outdoor tasks, and a bench stands near or against the tower. The courtyard also includes a woodshed/firewood storage area, a clothesline, and a rainwater collection barrel. The baseline specifies these physical facilities rather than current tools, laundry, stored quantities, or campaign-specific planting.
Feature: enclosing stone walls. Stone walls enclose the secluded outdoor courtyard, which wraps around part of the tower base.
Feature: LR access door. A normal door provides direct access to Heartstone LR, distinct from Heartstone's main exterior entrance.
Feature: training area and dummies. A training area occupies open space farther from the tower and contains training dummies.
Feature: medicinal planting beds. Two distinct planting areas contain beds intended for medicinal plants. Both areas are initially empty; baseline canon supplies no plants.
Feature: garden and tool shed. A shed in a perimeter area serves gardening and general outdoor tool storage; its initial inventory is unspecified.
Feature: practical work table. A table near the medicinal planting area supports practical outdoor tasks; no permanent tools or objects on it are specified.
Feature: tower-side bench. A bench stands near or against the tower, near the LR courtyard door.
Feature: woodshed and firewood storage. A woodshed/storage area near the garden/tool shed and tower accommodates stacked firewood; quantities are unspecified.
Feature: clothesline. A clothesline occupies a perimeter area and provides a place to hang laundry; current laundry is not baseline canon.
Feature: rainwater collection barrel. A barrel in a perimeter area serves rainwater collection; its current contents are unspecified.

Name: Heartstone Observation Floor
Display name: Heartstone F1
Aliases: Heartstone first upper floor; Heartstone observation floor; Heartstone recovery floor; F1
Type: location
Parent: Heartstone
Summary: Heartstone F1 is the first upper floor, a sparse open-plan private observation and recovery space with a normal maximum capacity of two patient beds.
Context: Heartstone F1 observation and recovery floor, patient beds, bedside stools and tables, wardrobes, medical cabinets, medicine storage.
F1 is one functional, open-plan observation and recovery floor inside Heartstone, without separate internal rooms. It is a simple private space, not an institutional medical facility. The continuous lateral spiral staircase arrives at the side/perimeter, leaving the central usable area open. It connects downward to LR and continues upward toward F2. The normal maximum physical patient capacity is two beds; capacity does not establish current occupancy. Each bed has one simple stool, one small bedside table/nightstand, and one wardrobe or tall storage cupboard intended for that bed. The wardrobes are initially empty. Opposite the patient-bed arrangement stand one or two large wooden medical-storage cabinets, also initially empty. Their intended future use is storing medicines, dressings, instruments, and ordinary medical supplies. The furnishings remain sparse; no current patients or medical inventory are specified.
Feature: two patient stations. Two patient beds provide the normal maximum physical capacity. Each bed has one simple bedside stool, one small bedside table/nightstand, and one wardrobe or tall storage cupboard intended for that bed. Both wardrobes are initially empty; capacity is not current occupancy.
Feature: wooden medical-storage cabinets. One or two large wooden cabinets stand on the opposite wall/side from the patient-bed arrangement. They are initially empty, intended for future medicine storage, dressings, instruments, and ordinary medical supplies; no inventory is established.
Feature: lateral spiral stair access. The continuous lateral/peripheral spiral staircase reaches F1 from the side/perimeter, leaving the central usable area open. It connects downward to LR and continues upward toward F2; it is not a central tower core.

Name: Heartstone Living Floor
Display name: Heartstone LR
Aliases: Heartstone living room; Heartstone ground floor; LR
Type: location
Parent: Heartstone
Summary: Heartstone LR is the tower's ground-level living floor: one large, rounded, roughly circular open-plan domestic space. Its kitchen and hearth seating area share the same floor without separate internal rooms.
Context: Heartstone LR living room, ground-level living floor, open-plan kitchen and hearth seating.
Heartstone LR is a broad open domestic space bounded by old stone tower walls. Its aged wooden floor is visibly old but remains solid and serviceable. A massive wooden main entrance provides normal access from the city/outside side. A second normal door, roughly opposite, leads directly to the secluded courtyard on the kitchen/table side. A large stone hearth stands along one side of the room, with a small hearthside alcove immediately beside it. Behind and to the left of its seating area, a large table stands near the kitchen, which occupies part of the same open space. The visible hatch near the kitchen side provides separate descending access to U1. The continuous spiral staircase is reached through a normal doorway/opening along LR's perimeter, away from the center, and rises toward F1 and onward through the upper floors to F6. Broad wall shelving occupies part of the perimeter near this stair side. Normal illumination comes from daylight through exactly three windows, candles, and the hearth when lit.
Feature: massive main entrance door. A massive, old, heavy wooden door provides normal access from the city/outside side, opposite the courtyard side. A small entrance zone/entry recess lies immediately inside, within LR.
Feature: courtyard door. A second normal door on the kitchen/table side lies roughly opposite the main entrance and leads directly to the courtyard; this is the only currently established normal direct access between LR and CY.
Feature: aged wooden floor and stone walls. A visibly old but solid and serviceable wooden floor and old stone tower walls enclose the broad, roughly circular open-plan space.
Feature: large stone hearth. A dominant large stone hearth/fireplace stands along one side of the roughly circular room and provides important warmth and light when burning.
Feature: hearthside alcove. A small physical alcove/recess lies immediately to one side of the hearth, within LR.
Feature: hearth seating area with large sofa. A large rug, large sofa, and at least one armchair stand in front of the hearth. The sofa occupies a broadly central position relative to the hearth.
Feature: large table. A large household table stands behind and to the left of the hearth/seating area, away from the main entrance near the kitchen side. It serves meals, communal eating, and convivial/shared household use; current food, tableware, and occupants are unspecified.
Feature: open kitchen area. The kitchen occupies a broad curved perimeter section around or near the large table, within the same open-plan floor; it is not a separate room.
Feature: visible U1 hatch. A large, obvious hatch/trapdoor near the lower/outer part of the kitchen/table side leads down to U1 by separate descending access. It is neither hidden nor concealed and is separate from the upper-floor spiral staircase; lower/outer is relative layout, not a compass direction.
Feature: continuous spiral staircase. A normal doorway/opening along LR's perimeter, away from the center, leads into the single continuous lateral/peripheral spiral staircase. It rises near the outer tower interior toward F1 and onward to F6, not through a central tower core; U1 is accessed separately.
Feature: entrance shoe rack. A large shoe rack near the main entrance is intended for leaving footwear when entering.
Feature: entrance equipment rack and bench. A long horizontal rack/bench/storage surface near the main entrance can hold tools, weapons, carried equipment, and miscellaneous items; current contents are unspecified.
Feature: wall shelving. A broad section of wall shelving occupies part of the perimeter near the stair-access side. It provides space for household objects, small possessions, and ordinary miscellaneous storage; no permanent contents are specified.
Feature: three round-arched windows. Exactly three modest, vertically oriented windows have rectangular lower bodies and rounded arched tops: one near the kitchen, one near the main entrance, and one roughly left of the hearth.
Feature: ordinary illumination. Daylight enters through the three windows; candles and the hearth when lit provide other normal illumination.

Name: Square outside Heartstone
Display name: Outside Heartstone
Aliases: square outside Heartstone; public square outside Heartstone
Type: location
Parent: Calderan
Summary: The public square/open public area immediately outside Heartstone Tower's main entrance, in the city.
Context: Public square or open area immediately outside Heartstone Tower's main entrance.
This public open area lies immediately outside Heartstone Tower. It is a public city space where ordinary citizens and passers-by may plausibly be present. Heartstone's massive main entrance opens directly onto it. No specific landmarks, establishments, street names, district placement, or navigation routes are established.
Feature: Heartstone main entrance. Heartstone's massive, old, heavy wooden main entrance faces this area and opens directly into LR.

Name: Heartstone Underground Level
Display name: Heartstone U1
Aliases: Heartstone underground level; Heartstone cellar; Heartstone basement; U1
Type: location
Parent: Heartstone
Summary: Heartstone U1 is one large stone underground space, broader than LR and the tower floors above. It is partly used for ordinary household storage; much remains comparatively unused and its full extent is not completely understood.
Context: Heartstone U1 underground storage level, cellar, stone pillars, central drain, old door and unexplored lower stairs.
U1 is accessed directly from LR through the large visible hatch and separate descending access, not through the upper-floor spiral staircase. Its floor, walls, and ceiling are entirely stone. The ceiling is lower than those of the upper floors, but the broad space is not inherently claustrophobic. Exact dimensions and geometry are unspecified. Only part of U1 is actively used, chiefly for storage; large portions remain comparatively unused. Storage shelves and furnishings serve ordinary household needs without fixed inventories or an assumption that every shelf is full. Its full extent is not completely understood or explored. A separate old door in the underground masonry opens onto additional stairs descending farther below U1. Those lower stairs remain unexplored, and what lies beyond is unknown.
Feature: stone floor, walls, and ceiling. One broad underground space is entirely constructed in stone, with a lower ceiling than the upper floors; exact dimensions and geometry are unspecified.
Feature: LR hatch access. Separate descending access connects U1 to the large visible hatch in LR; the upper-floor spiral staircase does not reach U1.
Feature: stone support pillars. Stone pillars support the underground construction.
Feature: arched masonry recesses and openings. Arched recesses/openings are present in the masonry; their further geometry is unspecified.
Feature: circular floor drain and grate. A large circular floor drain/grate lies near the central area.
Feature: wall storage shelves. Wall shelves/storage areas are intended for food, preserved goods, ordinary household supplies, common materials, and consumables such as candles; contents and quantities are unspecified.
Feature: barrels, crates, and storage furnishings. Ordinary barrels, crates, and storage furnishings support the partly used storage area; no fixed contents or quantities are specified.
Feature: old door and lower descending stairs. One separate old door in the underground masonry opens onto additional stairs descending farther below U1. Their destination and what lies beyond remain unknown and undefined.

Name: Humans
Type: world_lore
Summary: Humans are the predominant population in West.
Human social institutions dominate much of West's political structure. No universal human racial abilities or statistics are established.

Name: Inquisition
Type: faction
Parent: Church
Summary: The Inquisition is a powerful, feared national organ of the Church.
The Inquisition is institutionally intimidating and can operate through local presence when necessary. It may take interest in exceptional magic, Light/Shadow users, matters considered dangerous or religiously significant, and other issues later defined by doctrine. Its authority, secrecy, reputation, and power make it feared. Legal powers remain undefined; it is not established as omnipotent, unopposed, or purely evil. Interest and intervention depend on circumstances, not an automatic response to every rare spell.

Name: Ironbound
Aliases: The Fortress on the Edge
Type: location
Parent: West
Summary: Ironbound is a major fortified frontier city east of Calderan, on West's side of the West–Center border.
Ironbound's defensive and administrative role makes it more than a settlement near the frontier. Its massive fortress-gate character and heavy stone-and-iron fortifications block armed incursions and desert raids, bearing physical evidence of repeated violent border clashes. It is a major military filtering point with important customs and border-control functions, high political tension, and frequent contact with the consequences of skirmishes. Official enforcement and unofficial corruption coexist. Authorities may ignore, facilitate, or inadequately investigate slave caravans originating in raids and cross-border violence. Not every guard is corrupt, and not all slave traffic through Ironbound is legal. It belongs to West rather than being an independent nation or autonomous city-state.
Feature: fortified frontier city. Massive fortress-gate character, heavy stone-and-iron defenses, and visible damage from repeated clashes.
Feature: military and customs filtering point. Defensive and administrative border control on West's side of the frontier; official enforcement coexists with unofficial corruption.

Name: Khar-Dune
Type: location
Parent: Center
Summary: Khar-Dune is a fortified desert settlement in western/southwestern Center with major underground slave and contraband markets.
Khar-Dune lies relatively near the West frontier and Chained Bay region. It developed around a watering point for mercenary caravans, surrounded by thick lime/mud-brick walls, and grew in importance as unofficial West–Center conflict intensified. Desert raiders bring prisoners captured across the border. Intermediaries may obscure or falsify origin, clean provenance or records, and sell captives onward toward West merchants or labor sites, works, and pits associated with Zul-Rath/Center. Its underground markets include slaves, contraband, and illicit cross-border trade. Not every resident is criminal. No named gangs or complete criminal hierarchy are established.
Feature: fortified caravan watering point. Originally developed around water for mercenary caravans and enclosed by thick lime/mud-brick walls.
Feature: underground slave and contraband markets. Major illicit cross-border trade with intermediaries who may falsify captives' provenance before onward sale.

Name: Learned Arts Guild
Type: faction
Summary: A national guild encompassing learned and professional disciplines in West, including magic.
The Learned Arts Guild encompasses scholars, scribes, archivists, educated specialists, some physicians or apothecaries where appropriate, magical scholarship, and practicing mages. Literacy does not imply membership. Magic belongs within this broader learned sphere; there is no separate Mages Guild. Rare and powerful practicing mages often have considerable influence, but do not automatically rule the guild. Local branches may have representatives who collectively determine or select a national representative; selection methods remain undefined. Civic magistracy may overlap professionally or socially but is not a subordinate guild branch.

Name: Light and Shadow
Type: world_lore
Summary: Light and Shadow are exceptionally rare magical classifications, not moral alignments.
Light is not inherently good; Shadow is not inherently evil. Both are nearly legendary in ordinary experience, known more through stories, records, rumor, and rare cases than everyday observation. They may have unusual interactions or opposition with one another; no full combat matrix is established. Clearly identifiable public use may attract major attention: surprise, fear, distrust, rumor, withdrawal, institutional interest, reports to authorities, or investigation by Church/Inquisition-related actors. Responses depend on context; no spell automatically summons the Inquisition. No Light hero, Shadow villain, or required conflict is established.

Name: Magic
Type: world_lore
Summary: Magic is publicly known and real, but genuine practitioners are uncommon.
Magic is not an everyday ability. Ordinary elemental magic is neither impossible nor legendary, although genuine magic users remain rare. In a very large city, practicing mages might number in the low dozens or even roughly two hands' worth; this is a rough rarity guideline, not a demographic equation. Some respect magic, some fear it, and many unfamiliar with it distrust it. Mages often gain influence, social leverage, institutional importance, or positions associated with knowledge and power. This does not make every mage wealthy, noble, politically powerful, or a guild leader.

Name: Magical Subschools
Type: world_lore
Summary: Primary magical traditions can contain specialized subschools, styles, and branches.
Water-associated Ice or Tidal styles, Air-associated Wind, and Fire-associated Ash or Cinder are illustrative possibilities, not an exhaustive canonical taxonomy. New subschools may emerge during play. A mage need not belong to exactly one subschool.

Name: Calderan City Structure
Type: world_lore
Summary: Calderan, West's capital and main campaign city, has five conceptual districts: West, East, North, South, and Center.
Context: Calderan city districts, distinct from the nations West, Center, and East.
District themes describe predominant social/economic character, not exclusive zoning. West has poorer and harder living conditions, heavy/manual labor, greater crime, rougher establishments, slavery-related activity, and vulnerable populations; slave pens or markets may occur where established. Not every inhabitant is poor or criminal. East emphasizes commerce, markets, shops, workshops, artisans, merchants, and everyday trade; Merchants and Artisans may have strong operational presence. North emphasizes temples, religion, healing, physicians, herbalists, traditional medicine, charitable care, and religious healing claims. Competent physicians and herbal practitioners, sincere religious practitioners, ineffective treatments, superstition, and charlatans can coexist. Religion is not universally fraudulent and temple healing is not universally magical. South emphasizes garrison, City Guard, barracks/security activity, inns, taverns, travelers, stables, and transit services. Center emphasizes wealth, nobility, powerful households, administration, major institutional offices, local guild-branch headquarters, Church influence, and the Duke's political seat/residence toward the civic core. Core areas tend toward greater prestige without formal nested subdistricts. Shops may exist in West, taverns in Center, and temples outside North. No specific establishments, district boundaries, or navigation routes are established.

Name: Mana
Type: world_lore
Summary: Mana underlies magical exertion; every living person possesses it, but only a small minority can consciously use it for magic.
Possessing mana does not imply magical ability. Why some people can use it remains undefined: no genetic, divine, training, bloodline, racial, or aptitude-test explanation is established. Mana can be spent and recovered; storage or manipulation through other means may be established later. Nicco's intended maximum is 100; actual current mana is engine-authoritative and stays between zero and maximum. The player establishes attempted or known abilities; no fixed spellbook is established. Approximate expenditure anchors are 5 for minor/simple non-healing magic, such as harmless sparks for amusement; 25 for superficial healing; 50 for serious or complex healing, including deeper injury or infection; and 75 for major whole-body/systemic healing involving internal and external damage. These are consistency anchors, not fixed spell prices. The narrator may propose reasonable costs; runtime validates numbers. The only currently defined universal recovery is 25 per crossed world-day boundary, capped at maximum. A day is 1440 world minutes. Sleep or rest alone grants nothing. Other recovery must arise from established gameplay through explicit validated deltas; being low on mana does not justify free restoration. No specific recovery item, ritual, place, or technique is established.

Name: Merchants Guild
Type: faction
Summary: A national guild representing major organized commercial interests in West.
The Merchants Guild broadly represents trade, merchants, large commercial networks, market influence, and commercial interests. It may maintain local city branches with local representatives. Local representatives from major cities collectively determine or select a national representative; selection procedures remain undefined. Branches are parts of this national institution, not independent unrelated guilds. No monopolies or detailed law are established.

Name: Mist Sea
Type: location
Summary: Mist Sea lies broadly north of the known continent.
Mist Sea is the named northern surrounding sea. Its broad position is established; no exact maritime boundaries or supernatural properties are established.

Name: Mixed Ancestry
Type: world_lore
Summary: Mixed ancestry exists between established peoples.
Examples include Half-Elves, Human/Beastfolk ancestry, and other plausible combinations between established peoples. No detailed genetic rules, inheritance percentages, or mandatory trait outcomes are defined. Specific characters' ancestry is established individually.

Name: Nicco
Type: character
Summary: Nicco is the player character: a 35-year-old human man, newly transported into this world, lawful owner of Heartstone Tower, and a Light mage.
Context: Nicco player character, human man, Heartstone owner, Light mage, newly arrived from another world.
Nicco is a 35-year-old human man. He was transported into this world from another world approximately one day before the campaign begins, and he has essentially no prior lived knowledge of this world unless explicitly established later. On arrival he became the lawful owner/holder of Heartstone Tower. He is tall and overweight, with a few visible white hairs and very mild, early balding; no further appearance details are established. His magical affinity/school is Light. His currently known Light subschools are healing and sacrifice, understood only within the existing magic framework; no mechanics for sacrifice are established. Being a Light mage gives him no automatic knowledge of spells, institutions, lore, or magical theory. Nicco is the player character: his dialogue, thoughts, intentions, and deliberate actions are supplied only by the player.

Name: Major Peoples
Type: world_lore
Summary: The currently established major sapient peoples are Humans, Elves, Dwarves, Beastfolk, and people of mixed ancestry.
These categories do not exhaust all peoples that could ever exist. Future peoples may be established when needed; no additional peoples are currently authored.

Name: Sandspear
Type: location
Parent: Center
Summary: Sandspear is a southern Center desert/coastal stronghold centered on a massive solitary black-basalt tower, with corsair and mercenary-mariner activity.
The defining tower rises from the desert near the coast in far southern Center. Sandspear is violent and lightly regulated, dominated by navigator guilds/groups and warlords without a fixed detailed government. Its economy spans piracy, corsair warfare, mercenary service, and maritime disruption. Zul-Rath may employ or tolerate its forces to harass shipping and disrupt West trade without formal national war; not every corsair is a direct government soldier. Sandspear persistently rivals Blackwater over Chained Bay, Sorrow Sea, and nearby trading lanes. Competition includes smuggling, piracy/corsair action, extortion/protection, captured cargo, slave trafficking, and wartime spoils, sometimes producing bloody naval engagements. This rivalry does not establish formal West–Center naval war or a predetermined winner.
Feature: solitary black-basalt tower. A massive solitary black-basalt tower rises from the desert and defines the settlement.
Feature: corsair and mercenary-mariner stronghold. Violent, lightly regulated maritime activity spans piracy, corsair warfare, mercenary service, and shipping disruption.
Feature: navigator groups and warlords. Dominant social actors without a fully defined or rigid city government.
Feature: maritime rival. Blackwater

Name: The Silent Ocean
Type: location
Summary: The Silent Ocean lies broadly east of the known continent.
The Silent Ocean is the named eastern surrounding ocean. The name establishes no supernatural property or explanation; exact maritime boundaries remain undefined.

Name: Skardgard
Type: location
Parent: East
Summary: Skardgard is East's principal coastal city, farther southeast, with strong natural defenses and a maritime economy.
Difficult fjord-like coastal geography, dark stone fortifications, persistent ice conditions, and isolation make Skardgard extremely difficult to assault by sea, not literally impossible to conquer. Its economic and population associations include whalers, shipbuilders, experienced sailors, high-seas fishing, maritime trade, and extraction or trade of rare resources from ice-bound regions. The rare resources are not individually specified. Exact fleet numbers and naval strength remain undefined.
Feature: principal coastal city. East's major coastal urban center.
Feature: fjord-like coast and dark stone fortifications. Persistent ice, difficult coastal geography, and strong natural defenses make foreign naval assaults extremely difficult.
Feature: whaling, shipbuilding, and high-seas fishing. Experienced sailors support these activities and maritime trade, including rare resources from ice-bound regions.

Name: Sorrow Sea
Type: location
Summary: Sorrow Sea lies broadly west of the known continent.
Sorrow Sea is the named western surrounding sea. Blackwater and Sandspear contest maritime routes associated with it. No exact routes, maritime boundaries, or supernatural properties are established.

Name: Vaelrost
Type: location
Parent: East
Summary: Vaelrost is East's political capital and a major urban center deep in the cold, snow-dominated eastern nation.
Vaelrost lies farther east/northeast relative to Frostspire. Its internal government and culture remain deliberately underdefined. No ruler, dynasty, magical ice walls, or supernatural architecture is established.
Feature: capital of East. East's national political capital.

Name: West
Display name: West (nation)
Type: location
Parent: Known Continent
Summary: West is the western nation, broadly mild, temperate, and greener; Calderan is its capital.
Context: West nation on the known continent, distinct from Calderan's West District.
West directly borders Center but shares no direct land border with East. Climate is a broad tendency, not uniform everywhere. Its major mapped settlements are Calderan, Ironbound, Davenport, and Blackwater; they are not its only possible settlements. West's established monarchy, Dukes, local councils, national guilds, Church, and nationally legal slavery with local regulation remain in force. Frontier tension with Center involves skirmishes, raids, territorial incidents, feuds, localized clashes, and unofficial violence, not permanent formally declared total war. Blackwater is geographically within West but outside effective normal direct control. Calderan and Davenport hold the principal institutional control over West's legal slave market.
Feature: national capital. Calderan
Feature: land border with Center. West directly borders Center.
Feature: temperate regional climate. Broadly mild, temperate, and greener; local variation remains possible.

Name: West Governance
Type: world_lore
Summary: West is a monarchy: the Royal Family stands above Dukes governing major cities and their surrounding territories.
Each Duke is the primary local authority beneath the Crown, supported by a local council. The council may include local nobles, representatives of the three national guilds, and ecclesiastical representation; membership counts, voting, quorum, and exact constitutional powers remain undefined. Local nobles exist without a standardized tier taxonomy. The four major institutional power blocs are the Merchants Guild, Artisans Guild, Learned Arts Guild, and Church. The first three are national guilds; the Church is not a guild but has comparable political weight. Guilds may maintain city branches and local representatives, who collectively determine or select a national representative; selection methods and terms remain undefined. For major kingdom-wide matters the Crown may summon or consult Dukes, national representatives of the three guilds, and national Church representation. No permanent exact council or constitution is fixed. King, Queen, Princes, and Princesses are ordinary royal concepts, not named NPCs; succession law remains undefined.

Name: Slavery in West
Type: world_lore
Summary: Slavery is nationally legal throughout West, with cities able to regulate its operation and administration.
National legality and local regulation are the established framework; detailed laws remain undefined. The institution is particularly relevant to West's treatment of Beastfolk, but enslaved people can have other backgrounds. Not every Beastfolk is enslaved, and not every enslaved person is a Center war captive. Calderan and Davenport hold principal institutional monopoly/control over West's legal slave market. Frontier raids and captives may feed Ironbound and/or Khar-Dune networks, pass through legal or falsified processing, reach Calderan/Davenport markets, and move toward West destinations, plantations, or colonies. This is a broad possible flow, not a universal route or a simulation graph. Ironbound combines official border enforcement with unofficial corruption; its slave traffic is not all legal. Khar-Dune intermediaries may falsify provenance. Blackwater is especially associated with illegal/unregistered trafficking, kidnapping, smuggling, and stolen captives; Sandspear may participate through corsair/criminal networks. Legal processing does not establish a lawful origin for every captive. Plantations and colonies exist within West's broader economic system, but their locations, sizes, ownership, crops, and political status remain undefined.

Name: Zul-Rath
Type: location
Parent: Center
Summary: Zul-Rath is Center's capital and major political center in the arid nation's northern/central interior.
Zul-Rath participates indirectly in Center's wider economic and military system. It may employ or tolerate forces such as Sandspear's corsairs when useful, including disruption of shipping and West trade without formal national war. Khar-Dune intermediaries may route captives toward labor sites, works, or pits associated with Zul-Rath or Center. Its ruler, dynasty, government system, districts, religion, exact architecture, detailed economy, and demographics remain undefined.
Feature: capital of Center. Center's major national political center.
